questions.question: Should <iframe src> stay in the covered set?
questions.why: It is the covered row with the most plausible benign carrier - a documentation page embedding a player (T46-corpus.ts Part B, docsPageWithIframe). It was covered because a page carries no iframe unless it deliberately embeds one, so its incidence is content-dependent rather than file-dependent, and because leaving the canonical alternative to open would make the rest of the coverage decorative. A reviewer should agree with that rather than inherit it; it is one line in FETCHING_ATTRIBUTES to revert.

options.label: Keep it covered; the allowlist is the remedy, exactly as for
Move it to the deferred set with the same default-allowlist prerequisite as <script src> and <link href>

questions.question: What should the floor's default egress allowlist contain?
questions.why: This is the single named prerequisite for the four deferred surfaces (<script src>, <link href>/<link imagesrcset>, CSS destinations, <iframe srcdoc>). The floor's default allowlist is empty, so deny-by-default equals deny-everything for a document's own infrastructure, and covering those surfaces today would mask URLs inside source a tool was asked to show. It is a product decision outside src/security/detect/exfil.ts and outside this task's ownership.

questions.question: Is the policies.md edit within the 'if and only if the current wording is inaccurate' clause?
questions.why: The package described the redaction norm and said nothing at all about the auto-fetch floor's surface coverage, so the limitation existed only in flow artifacts and a reader was free to conclude the floor was total. That silence was treated as the inaccuracy. If the orchestrator reads the clause more narrowly, the addition is one contiguous subsection and one version line. The separate, precise note about the norm's own credential-locator sentence (T46-implementation.md section 7, last paragraph) is offered and deliberately not applied.
